Class TextStyles

java.lang.Object
dev.visdb.seesaw.decorators.TextStyles
public class TextStyles extends Object
This class manages a hierarchy of named TextStyles; a TextStyle is an AttributeSet with a limited list of attribute names, see below. There are methods to apply an AttributeSet to either a JTextCompoent or JTextArea.

The styles are usually read from a resource/file. After styles are loaded, then executeFullStyleDiagnostics(boolean) is run and results logged. If there's an exception/error during loading and/or diagnostics fail then the load is backed out. See TextStyles.LoadStatus.

Other than the methods that operate on JTextComponents only getStyleNames() and getStyle(java.lang.String) can be called from the EventQueue. If a method is called from an inappropriate thread an IllegalStateException is thrown. 

Attributes in a TextStyle
Attribute Name Acceptable Values Default Target Component
foreground Color: #ff2277, name BLACK JComponent
background Color: #ff2277, name WHITE JComponent
opaque true,false true JComponent
fontFamily String "Monospaced" JComponent
fontSize int 12 JComponent
bold true, false false JComponent
italic true, false false JComponent
underline true, false false JComponent
strikethrough true, false false JComponent
alignment "left", "center", "right" "left" JTextField
linewrap true, false false JTextArea
wordwrap true, false false JTextArea
scrollbars "both", "vertical", "horizontal",
"asneeded", "none" 		"asneeded" JTextArea
autoscroll true, false ignore JTextArea

  • There are two special words, "keep" and "default", which are acceptable values for any style attribute. "keep" means that the current component value be unaltered when the style is applied. "default" means use the default value.
  • If an attribute is not specified, then "keep" is assumed.
  • If a color starts with "#" try Color.decode(String); if not try matching the value to a name of a color as seen in Color's fields.
  • If a style is applied to a component, and the style has attributes that are not applicable to the component, the inapplicable attributes are ignored.
  • The scroll related styles are only applied if the JTextArea is embedded in a ScrollPane
There are two supported formats for specifying styles, json and properties. 
# comments allowed in json             |
{                                      |
  "default": {                         |
    "foreground": "#333333",           |      default.foreground=#333333
    "background": "#FFFFFF",           |      default.background=#FFFFFF
    "fontFamily": "Monospaced",        |      default.fontFamily=Monospaced
    "fontSize": 16,                    |      default.fontSize=16
    "alignment": "left"                |      default.alignment=left
  },                                   |
  "warning": {                         |
    "inherits": "default",             |      warning.inherits=default
    "background": "#FFF3CD",           |      warning.background=#FFF3CD
    "alignment": "center"              |      warning.alignment=center
  },                                   |
  "criticalError": {                   |
    "inherits": "warning",             |      criticalError.inherits=warning
    "alignment": "right",              |      criticalError.alignment=right
    "foreground": "#721C24",           |      criticalError.foreground=#721C24
    "strikethrough": true,             |      criticalError.strikethrough=true
    "underline": "default"             |      criticalError.underline=default
  }                                    |
}                                      |
Each produces, as displayed by generateDiagnosticTrees(StringBuilder): 
Resolved Structural Hierarchy Trees:
└── default
      • foreground = java.awt.Color[r=51,g=51,b=51]
      • background = java.awt.Color[r=255,g=255,b=255]
      • family = Monospaced
      • size = 16
      • alignment = left
    └── warning
          • background = java.awt.Color[r=255,g=243,b=205]
          • alignment = center
        └── criticalError
              • alignment = right
              • foreground = java.awt.Color[r=114,g=28,b=36]
              • strikethrough = true
              • underline = default
